From 7bb09315f93dce6acc54bf59e5a95ba7365c2be4 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Hyunwoo Kim <imv4bel@gmail.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 18:40:36 +0900
Subject: [PATCH] tls: Fix race condition in tls_sw_cancel_work_tx()

This issue was discovered during a code audit.

After cancel_delayed_work_sync() is called from tls_sk_proto_close(),
tx_work_handler() can still be scheduled from paths such as the
Delayed ACK handler or ksoftirqd.
As a result, the tx_work_handler() worker may dereference a freed
TLS object.

The following is a simple race scenario:

          cpu0                         cpu1

tls_sk_proto_close()
  tls_sw_cancel_work_tx()
                                 tls_write_space()
                                   tls_sw_write_space()
                                     if (!test_and_set_bit(BIT_TX_SCHEDULED, &tx_ctx->tx_bitmask))
    set_bit(BIT_TX_SCHEDULED, &ctx->tx_bitmask);
    cancel_delayed_work_sync(&ctx->tx_work.work);
                                     schedule_delayed_work(&tx_ctx->tx_work.work, 0);

To prevent this race condition, cancel_delayed_work_sync() is
replaced with disable_delayed_work_sync().

Fixes: f87e62d45e51 ("net/tls: remove close callback sock unlock/lock around TX work flush")
Signed-off-by: Hyunwoo Kim <imv4bel@gmail.com>
Reviewed-by: Simon Horman <horms@kernel.org>
Reviewed-by: Sabrina Dubroca <sd@queasysnail.net>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/aZgsFO6nfylfvLE7@v4bel
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

diff --git a/net/tls/tls_sw.c b/net/tls/tls_sw.c
index 9937d4c810f2..b1fa62de9dab 100644
--- a/net/tls/tls_sw.c
+++ b/net/tls/tls_sw.c
@@ -2533,7 +2533,7 @@ void tls_sw_cancel_work_tx(struct tls_context *tls_ctx)
 
 	set_bit(BIT_TX_CLOSING, &ctx->tx_bitmask);
 	set_bit(BIT_TX_SCHEDULED, &ctx->tx_bitmask);
-	cancel_delayed_work_sync(&ctx->tx_work.work);
+	disable_delayed_work_sync(&ctx->tx_work.work);
 }
 
 void tls_sw_release_resources_tx(struct sock *sk)
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Modifications

The patch fixes a race condition in the TLS (Transport Layer Security) software implementation, specifically in the `tls_sw_cancel_work_tx()` function. The issue arises because `cancel_delayed_work_sync()` only cancels any pending delayed work but does not prevent the work item from being rescheduled later (e.g., via a concurrent `schedule_delayed_work` from another execution path). This can lead to a use-after-free when the work handler operates on a already freed TLS context.

### Modifications per file:

- **net/tls/tls_sw.c** – `tls_sw_cancel_work_tx()`:
  - Replaced `cancel_delayed_work_sync(&ctx->tx_work.work)` with `disable_delayed_work_sync(&ctx->tx_work.work)`.
  - This change ensures that after the function is called (typically during socket close), the delayed work is not only cancelled but also disabled, preventing any subsequent rescheduling attempts. The `disable_delayed_work_sync()` function atomically cancels any pending work and marks the work as disabled, so future calls to `schedule_delayed_work` will have no effect.

### Relationships:

Since only one file is modified, the relationship is straightforward: the bug fix is entirely contained within the `tls_sw.c` file. The change directly addresses the race condition between the close path (calling `tls_sw_cancel_work_tx`) and the write-space callback path (calling `tls_sw_write_space` which may schedule the delayed work). By using `disable_delayed_work_sync` instead of `cancel_delayed_work_sync`, the rescheduling of the work after cancellation is prevented, thus eliminating the race.

Here is the commit message:
tls: Fix race condition in tls_sw_cancel_work_tx()

This issue was discovered during a code audit.

After cancel_delayed_work_sync() is called from tls_sk_proto_close(),
tx_work_handler() can still be scheduled from paths such as the
Delayed ACK handler or ksoftirqd.
As a result, the tx_work_handler() worker may dereference a freed
TLS object.

The following is a simple race scenario:

          cpu0                         cpu1

tls_sk_proto_close()
  tls_sw_cancel_work_tx()
                                 tls_write_space()
                                   tls_sw_write_space()
                                     if (!test_and_set_bit(BIT_TX_SCHEDULED, &tx_ctx->tx_bitmask))
    set_bit(BIT_TX_SCHEDULED, &ctx->tx_bitmask);
    cancel_delayed_work_sync(&ctx->tx_work.work);
                                     schedule_delayed_work(&tx_ctx->tx_work.work, 0);

To prevent this race condition, cancel_delayed_work_sync() is
replaced with disable_delayed_work_sync().

Fixes: f87e62d45e51 ("net/tls: remove close callback sock unlock/lock around TX work flush")
Signed-off-by: Hyunwoo Kim <imv4bel@gmail.com>
Reviewed-by: Simon Horman <horms@kernel.org>
Reviewed-by: Sabrina Dubroca <sd@queasysnail.net>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/aZgsFO6nfylfvLE7@v4bel
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

Here is the root cause:
In tls_sw_cancel_work_tx(), cancel_delayed_work_sync() only stops the currently pending delayed work but does not prevent the work from being rescheduled afterwards. A concurrent tls_sw_write_space() can test_and_set_bit(BIT_TX_SCHEDULED) and then call schedule_delayed_work() after the cancel, causing the work handler to run on a freed TLS object, leading to a use-after-free race condition.

Here is the patch:
 
 void tls_sw_cancel_work_tx(struct tls_context *tls_ctx)
 {
 	struct tls_sw_context_tx *ctx = tls_sw_ctx_tx(tls_ctx);
 
 	set_bit(BIT_TX_CLOSING, &ctx->tx_bitmask);
 	set_bit(BIT_TX_SCHEDULED, &ctx->tx_bitmask);
-	cancel_delayed_work_sync(&ctx->tx_work.work);
+	disable_delayed_work_sync(&ctx->tx_work.work);
 }
